verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              प्रविशन्नर्जुनो राजन्नाश्रमं सत्यवादिनः। ददर्शासीनमेकान्ते मुनिं सत्यवतीसुतम्॥१॥
स तमासाद्य धर्मज्ञमुपतस्थे महाव्रतम्। अर्जुनोऽस्मीति नामास्मै निवेद्याभ्यवदत्ततः॥२॥
verses.english: Approaching that Rishi of high vows and gifted with a knowledge of al duties, he said, 'I am Arjuna'-~and then awaited his pleasure.

verses.sanskrit: स्वागतं तेऽस्त्विति प्राह मुनिः सत्यवतीसुतः। आस्यतामिति होवाच प्रसन्नात्मा महामुनिः॥३॥
verses.english: Satyavati's son, endued with high penances, answered, saying, "Welcome!' Of tranquil soul the great ascetic further said, 'Take our seat.'

verses.sanskrit: तमप्रतीतमनसं निःश्वसन्तं पुनः पुनः। निर्विण्णमनसं दृष्ट्वा पार्थं व्यासोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥४॥
verses.english: Seeing that the son of Pritha was greatly cheerless and breathing heavy sighs repeatedly and filled with despair, Vyasa, addressed him, saying——Have you been sprinkled with water from anybody's nails or hair or the end of anybody's cloth, or from the mouth of a jar? Did you know any woman before the cessation of her menses? Have you killed a Brahmana?

verses.sanskrit: नखकेशदशाकुम्भवारिणा किं समुक्षितः। आवीरजानुगमनं ब्राह्मणो वा हतस्त्वया॥५॥
युद्धे पराजितो वाऽसि गतश्रीरिव लक्ष्यसे। न त्वां प्रभिन्नं जानामि किमिदं भरतर्षभ॥६॥
verses.english: Have you been defeated in battle? You look like one shorn of prosperity! I do not know that you have been defeated by any one. Why then, O chief Bharata's race, this exceedingly dejected look! You should O of Pritha, tell me all, if, indeed, there be no harm in telling it.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रोतव्यं चेन्मया पार्थ क्षिप्रमाख्यातुमर्हसि।
              अर्जुन उवाच।
              यः स मेघवपुः श्रीमान् बृहत्पङ्कजलोचनः॥७॥
verses.english: Arjuna said He whose complexion was like that of a cloud, he whose eyes were like pair of large lotus petals, viz., Krishna has, with Rama, renounced his body and ascended to heaven.

verses.sanskrit: स कृष्णः सह रामेण त्यक्त्वा देहं दिवं गतः। मौसले वृष्णिवीराणां विनाशो ब्रह्मशापजः॥८॥
बभूव वीरान्तकरः प्रभासे लोमहर्षणः। एते शूरा महात्मानः सिंहदर्पा महाबलाः॥९॥
verses.english: At Prabhasa, through iron bolts caused by the curse denounced by Brahmanas, the destruction has taken place of the Vrishni heroes. That destruction has been awful and not even a single hero has escaped,

verses.sanskrit: भोजवृष्ण्यन्धका ब्रह्मन्नन्योन्यं तैर्हतं युधि। गदापरिघशक्तीनां सहाः परिघबाहवः॥१०॥
verses.english: The heroes of the Bhoja, the Andhaka, and the Vrishni races, O Brahmana, who were all gifted with high-souls, great might, and leonine pride, have killed one another in battle. Possessed of arms which looked like maces of iron, and capable of bearing the strokes of heavy clubs and darts, alas they have all been killed with blades of Eraka grass. See the perverse course of Time. Five hundred thousand mighty-armed warriors have thus been killed. Encountering one another, they have met with destruction.

verses.sanskrit: त एरकाभिर्निहिताः पश्य कालस्य पर्ययम्। हतं पञ्चशतं तेषां सहस्रं बाहुशालिनाम्॥११॥
निधनं समनुप्राप्तं समासाद्येतरेतरम्। पुनः पुनर्न मृष्यामि विनाशममितौजसाम्॥१२॥
चिन्तयानो यदूनां च कृष्णस्य च यशस्विनः। शोषणं सागरस्येव पर्वतस्येव चालनम्॥१३॥
verses.english: Thinking repeatedly of this destruction of the Yadava warriors of immeasurable energy and of the illustrious Krishna, I cannot get peace of mind.

verses.sanskrit: नभसः पतनं चैव शैत्यमग्नेस्तथैव च। अश्रद्धेयमहं मन्ये विनाशं शार्ङ्गधन्वनः॥१४॥
verses.english: The death of the holder of Sharnga is as incredible as the drying up of the ocean, the displacement of a mountain, the falling down of the heaven, or the cooling property of fie. Deprived of the company of the Vrishni heroes, I wish not to live in this world.

verses.sanskrit: न चेह स्थातुमिच्छामि लोके कृष्णविनाकृतः। इतः कष्टतरं चान्यच्छृणु तद्वै तपोधन॥१५॥
मनो मे दीर्यते येन चिन्तयानस्य वै मुहुः। पश्यतो वृष्णिदाराश्च मम ब्रह्मन् सहस्रशः॥१६॥
verses.english: Another event has taken place that is more painful than this, O you having penances for wealth. Repeatedly thinking of it, my heart is breaking.

verses.sanskrit: आभीरैरनुसृत्याजौ हृताः पञ्चनदालयैः। धनुरादाय तत्राहं नाशकं तस्य पूरणे॥१७॥
verses.english: In my very sight, O Brahmana, thousands of Vrishni ladies were carried away by the Abhiras of the country of the five waters, who attacked us.

verses.sanskrit: यथा पुरा च मे वीर्यं भुजयोर्न तथाऽभवत्। अस्त्राणि मे प्रनष्टानि त्रिविधानि महामुने॥१८॥
verses.english: Taking up my bow, I found myself unequal to even string it. The power that had existed in my arms seemed to have disappeared on that occasion.

verses.sanskrit: शराश्च क्षयमापन्नाः क्षणेनैव समन्ततः। पुरुषश्चाप्रमेयात्मा शङ्खचक्रगदाधरः॥१९॥
verses.english: O great ascetic, my weapons of various kinds failed to appear. Soon, again, my arrows became exhausted.

verses.sanskrit: चतुर्भुजः पीतवासाः श्यामः पद्मदलेक्षणः। यश्च याति पुरस्तान्मे रथस्य सुमहाद्युतिः॥२०॥
verses.english: That person of immeasurable soul, of four arms, holding the conch, the discus, and the mace, clad in yellow robes, dark of complexion, and possessing eyes resembling lotus-petals, is no longer seen by me! Alas, reft of Govinda, what have I to live for, dragging my life in sorrow?

verses.sanskrit: प्रदहन् रिपुसैन्यानि न पश्याम्यहमच्युतम्। येन पूर्वं प्रदग्धानि शत्रुसैन्यानि तेजसा॥२१॥
verses.english: He who used to stalk in advance of my car, that divine form gifted with great splendour and unfading power, consuming as he proceeded all hostile warriors, can no longer be seen by me.

verses.sanskrit: शरैर्गाण्डीवनिर्मुक्तैरहं पश्चाच्च नाशयम्। तमपश्यन्विषीदामि घूर्णामीव च सत्तम॥२२॥
verses.english: No longer seeing him who by his energy first burnt all hostile troops whom I afterwards killed with arrows shot off Gandiva, I am filled with grief and my head swims, O best of men! Penetrated with cheerlessness and despair, I cannot get peace of mind.

verses.sanskrit: परिनिर्विण्णचेताश्च शान्ति नोपलभेऽपि च। विना जनार्दनं वीरं नाहं जीवितुमुत्सहे॥२३॥
verses.english: I dare not live, reft of the heroic Janardana. As soon as I heard that Vishnu had left the earth, my eyes became dim and all things disappeared from my vision.

verses.sanskrit: श्रुत्वैव हि गतं विष्णुं ममापि मुमुहुर्दिशः। प्रनष्टज्ञातिवीर्यस्य शून्यस्य परिधावतः॥२४॥

उपदेष्टुं मम श्रेयो भवानर्हति सत्तम।
              व्यास उवाच।
              ब्रह्मशापविनिर्दग्धा वृष्ण्यन्धकमहारथाः॥२५॥
विनष्टाः कुरुशार्दूल न तान् शोचितुमर्हसि। भवितव्यं तथा तच्च दिष्टमेतन्महात्मनाम्॥२६॥
verses.english: Vyasa said The powerful car-warriors of the Vrishni and the Andhaka races have all been consumed by the Brahmanas' course. O chief of Kuru's race, you should not grieve for their destruction.

verses.sanskrit: उपेक्षितं च कृष्णेन शक्तेनापि व्यपोहितुम्। त्रैलोक्यमपि गोविंदः कृत्स्नं स्थावरजङ्गमम्॥२७॥
verses.english: That which has taken place, had been ordained. It was the destiny of those great warriors. Krishna allowed it to take place although he was fully competent to befell it.

verses.sanskrit: प्रसहेदन्यथाकर्तुं कुतः शापं महात्मनाम्। रथस्य पुरतो याति यः सचक्रगदाधरः॥२८॥
verses.english: Govinda was able to after the very course of the universe with all its mobile and immobile creatures. What need then be said of the curse of even great Brahmanas?

verses.sanskrit: तव स्नेहात्पुराणर्षिर्वासुदेवश्चतुर्भुजः। कृत्वा भारावतरणं पृथिव्याः पृथुलोचनः॥२९॥
verses.english: for you He who used to proceed in front of your car, arined with discus and mace, through affection was the four-armed Vasudeva, that ancient Rishi.

verses.sanskrit: मोक्षयित्वा तनुं प्राप्तः कृष्णः स्वस्थानमुत्तमम्। त्वयाऽपीह महत्कर्म देवानां पुरुषर्षभ॥३०॥
verses.english: That great one of expansive eyes, viz., Krishna, having lightened the burthen of the Earth and cast off his (human) body, has attained to his own high seat.

verses.sanskrit: कृतं भीमसहायेन यमाभ्यां च महाभुज। कृतकृत्यांश्च वो मन्ये संसिद्धान्कुरुपुङ्गव॥३१॥
verses.english: By you also, O foremost of men, with Bhima for your helpmate and the twins, O mighty-armed hero, has the great work of the gods been done.

verses.sanskrit: गमनं प्राप्तकालं व इदं श्रेयस्करं विभो। एवं बुद्धिश्च तेजश्च प्रतिपत्तिश्च भारत॥३२॥
verses.english: O foremost one of Kuru's race, I regard you and your brothers as crowned with success, for you have accomplished the great purpose of your lives! The Time has come for your departure from the world. Even this, O powerful one, is what is beneficial for you now.

verses.sanskrit: भवन्ति भवकालेषु विपद्यन्ते विपर्यये। कालमूलमिदं सर्वं जगद्बीजं धनञ्जय॥३३॥
verses.english: Even thus, understanding and prowess and foresight. O Bharata, arise when days of prosperity have gone. These very acquisitions disappear when the hour of adversity comes.

verses.sanskrit: काल एव समादत्ते पुनरेव यदृच्छया। स एव बलवान्भूत्वा पुनर्भवति दुर्बलः॥३४॥
verses.english: All this has Time for its root. Time is, indeed, the seed of the of the universe, O not FINISH MA Dhananjaya! It is Time, again, which withdraws everything at its pleasure.

verses.sanskrit: स एवेशश्च भूत्वेह परैराज्ञाप्यते पुनः। कृतकृत्यानि चास्त्राणि गतान्यद्य यथागतम्॥३५॥
verses.english: One becomes powerful, and, again, losing that power, becomes weak. One becomes a master and rules others, and again, losing that position, becomes a servant for obeying the order of others.

verses.sanskrit: पुनरेष्यन्ति ते हस्ते यदा कालो भविष्यति। कालो गन्तुं गतिं मुख्यां भवतामपि भारत॥३६॥
verses.english: Your weapons, having achieved success, have gone away to the place they came from. They will, again, come into your hands when the Time for their coming approaches.

verses.sanskrit:
एतच्छ्रेयो हि वो मन्ये परमं भरतर्षभ।
              वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एतद्वचनमाज्ञाय व्यासस्यामिततेजसः॥३७॥
verses.english: The Time has come, O Bharata, for you all to attain to the highest end. This is what I consider to be highly beneficial for you all, O chief of Bharata's race.

verses.sanskrit: अनुज्ञातो ययौ पार्थो नगरं नागसाह्वयम्। प्रविश्य च पुरी वीरा समासाद्य युधिष्ठिरम्। आचष्ट तद्यथावृत्तं वृष्ण्यन्धककुलं प्रति॥३८॥
